payload.text: Zelie's request (in French): be a horse doing competitions/missions, ride ON the horse seeing its ears and head, obstacles, speed up/slow down, jump at the right moment, steer left/right to choose your path, in a carriere (riding arena), choosable horse color and place. Engine: three.js ('3djs').

The game is a static artifact at zelie/index.html, not a self capability: the kernel forbids projections from emitting JavaScript, so a three.js game cannot be a projection. The design organ lives in self; the game lives beside it.

The design organ is a lesson (lessons/zelie-design) because events.jsonl is never committed: the durable, committable form of this design log is the lesson's record.jsonl, exported at the end with 'self give design.' so any clone can learn the full build history.
Tried to load three.js from CDN (cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com): the sandbox network policy answers 403 to CONNECT. A CDN import in the game would also break offline play for a kid on a tablet.

Vendor three.module.min.js 0.160.0 into zelie/, extracted from the npm registry tarball (registry.npmjs.org is allowed directly). The game is fully self-contained and works offline from a file:// open or any static server.

Playtested headlessly: playwright-core driving the preinstalled Chromium against file://zelie/index.html — screenshots at menu/start/gallop/jump/finish plus state assertions. A blind autopilot run finished the course: mode 'fini', 1 clean jump, 4 faults, zero console errors.

First single-file build broke: rewriting three's trailing export{} into window.THREE={} and pasting it as a classic script put its minified top-level bindings (it uses $) into the shared global lexical scope, colliding with the game's own 'const $'. Fixed by wrapping the rewritten three source in an IIFE.

First rider camera (0, 2.05, 0) with a thick withers cylinder 0.45m ahead: the neck filled the bottom half of the screen as a giant blob and the head sat above the horizon, hiding the obstacles. Fixed: camera up and back (0, 2.3, 0.5) pitched slightly down, slimmer lower neck, head pitched down so you look over it between the ears.
The HUD chronometer stayed at 0.0s the whole course: it was only refreshed in majHud(), which runs when an obstacle is judged. Moved the chrono update into the frame loop.

The riding view sells 'tu es SUR le cheval': ears (cones, they flick on their own), head seen from above between them, forelock and mane in the mane color, reins running from the rider's hands to the head. Gallop bob scales with speed; the neck stretches forward during a jump; a small camera dip on landing.

Gameplay is real show-jumping rules tuned for a child: a fallen bar = 4 faults (the bar visibly drops and rolls, the horse slows), clearance is forgiving (clears if belly height > bar height minus 0.35m — the legs tuck), and results give 3 stars for sans-faute, 2 up to 4 faults, 1 beyond. Nothing ever kills you; the worst outcome is a message and a slower horse.

The course is 3 lanes (gauche/milieu/droite); each obstacle line blocks 1-3 lanes depending on mission. Layout comes from a deterministic pseudo-random function of (mission, line), so each mission is the SAME course on every replay — a child can learn it. Missions: Premier concours (6 obstacles, bars 0.85m), Concours regional (8, 1.0m), Grand Prix (10, 1.15m).

UI entirely in French. Choices before riding: 5 robes (alezan, noir, blanc, gris pommele, palomino) and 3 lieux (carriere, plage avec la mer, foret dense). Controls: arrows + space on keyboard, and on-screen touch buttons (steer, tortoise/horse for speed, big SAUTE! button) for a tablet.

All sound is synthesized in WebAudio at runtime — hoofbeats are filtered noise bursts locked to the gallop bob cycle, success is a two-note ding, a knock is a low thud. No audio files to load, nothing to fetch.

Round-tripped the lesson: a fresh SELF_HOME learning lessons/zelie-design deposited all 14 design.noted events verbatim, doors re-stamped learn:zelie-design, plus the intent.declared and the lesson.learned receipt. The design log travels.
